question: For Asian-Indian patients, bariatric surgery is indicated at a BMI ≥37.5 kg/m² (without obesity-related comorbidities) OR at BMI ≥32.5 kg/m² when at least one significant obesity-related comorbidity such as type 2 diabetes or hypertension is present — thresholds that are lower than the conventional Western criteria.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Asian-Indian bariatric surgery thresholds are lower than Western criteria: ≥37.5 kg/m² without comorbidities (vs Western ≥40), or ≥32.5 kg/m² with at least one significant comorbidity (vs Western ≥35), reflecting the higher metabolic risk at lower BMI in South Asians.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Asian-Indian bariatric thresholds are lower than Western ones (BMI ≥40 without comorbidity, ≥35 with comorbidity) because metabolic risk occurs at lower BMI in South Asians. The IDF/Indian guidelines endorse BMI ≥37.5 (no comorbidity) or ≥32.5 (with comorbidity) for surgical referral.
